source: Aswath Damodaran, corporate finance lecture packet (cfpacket2spr20), pages 222-223.
refresh: Re-estimate on current data where possible: https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/ publishes the underlying cross-section each January, and the coefficients drift with the market environment. These are a January 2014 snapshot fitted on US firms only; payout norms differ enormously by region. Pass a refreshed file with regressions_path rather than editing this copy.
caveat: Both equations are fitted on dividends alone. A firm returning cash through buybacks shows a large negative gap and is wrongly labelled a cash hoarder. Always add buybacks back before acting on the gap.

inputs.BETA: Company beta, preferably bottom-up, as a decimal.
inputs.EGR: Expected growth rate in earnings over the next 5 years, as a decimal (0.1473, not 14.73).
inputs.DCAP: Total debt / (total debt + market value of equity), as a decimal.

payout.dependent: Dividends / Net Income, as a decimal

yield.dependent: Dividends / Current Price, as a decimal

sign_interpretation.BETA: Negative. Riskier firms pay out less, because committing to a dividend when cash flows are volatile is dangerous.
sign_interpretation.EGR: Negative. High-growth firms need their cash; this is the life-cycle result in regression form.
sign_interpretation.DCAP: Positive. More levered firms pay higher dividends and yields in the data.
